_comment: The EMPIRE / Williams 20-Year Plan MSP buy box, encoded so the scanner can score strategic fit — not just market valuation. Deal 1 is a Dallas-based platform acquisition (H2 2031) financed SBA 7(a) + seller note (~$700K equity in), operated on an AI-native model with a legal-vertical edge, bought at ~3-4.5x and re-rated to 8-12x at exit. Tuck-ins follow at 2.5-3.5x SDE. Edit these to change how deals are ranked.

geography.principle: For a Dallas-run, AI-native, remote-capable MSP, what matters is CUSTOMER REACH and remote-operability — not the seller's HQ city. A College Station shop serving clients across Texas or multiple states is fully operable from Dallas; a shop whose clients are all one local market and onsite-dependent ties you to that market. HQ metro is a minor plus (density/relationships), never a gate. Employee count and how many are onshore/local and will transfer are separate diligence facts that this profile flags but rarely has data for.
geography.note: geo points = reachMultiplier × the onshoreGeo weight. A broad/remote customer base outranks HQ location because it's operable from Dallas; home-metro (DFW) adds only a small bonus.

platformWindow.comment: Earnings on either basis. Sweet spot $1.0-1.5M EBITDA. 'Structure 1' (max 7(a) + seller note + equity) stretches the ceiling to ~$1.8M EBITDA only if the seller carries a full note and the multiple stays disciplined; above that the business price clears the financeable envelope.

priceDiscipline.marketRealityNote: $1-3M EBITDA MSPs clear at 5-8x with consolidators; a 4.75-5x SBA-financed offer only wins off-market or with a seller who values certainty/legacy over top dollar.

capitalStack.comment: Structure 1: Max 7(a) + seller note + your equity. Real estate, if any, rides a SEPARATE 504/CRE loan outside the 7(a) and does not consume this envelope.
capitalStack.envelopeNote: sbaCap $5M + sellerNoteMax $1M + equityCashMax $0.7M = ~$6.7M business price (image says ~$6.5-7M). Half the 10% equity injection can be seller standby paper, so cash goes further.

realEstatePolicy.preference: minimize — MSPs are asset-light; you don't want to be a landlord for its own sake
realEstatePolicy.whenWorthIt: only if an owned building comes attached to a genuinely great business, and financing it separately (504/CRE, ~85% LTV, outside the 7(a)) is what makes the blended deal pencil or lifts the ceiling
realEstatePolicy.effect: a separately-financed RE component raises total deal capacity without eating the $6.7M business envelope

sellerFinancingPolicy.why: A seller carrying paper both stretches your cash equity AND signals conviction in the business post-close. Availability and terms are a top-3 diligence item on every candidate.
sellerFinancingPolicy.unknownIsRisk: Where seller financing is unconfirmed, treat it as an open question that materially affects whether the deal is financeable at all.

requirements.gmInPlace: non-negotiable — a GM/service manager who owns client relationships so the owner can exit

verticalTiebreaker.note: Generalist chassis with vertical concentration beats a vertical-only identity. Chassis quality outweighs vertical fit for Deal 1.

operatingThesis.aiMarginUplift: Agentic ticket triage, auto-documentation, and L1 auto-resolution move gross margin from the industry's 10-15% toward ~35%. Re-rate upside lives in contractual MRR you can protect while AI takes out L1 labor — NOT in book-of-hours or resale revenue.
operatingThesis.reRate: Buy at ~3x, re-rate to 8-12x EBITDA at a 2039-41 exit/recap.
operatingThesis.onshoreThesis: The plan's edge is a legal / professional-services vertical (confidentiality- and compliance-sensitive buyers) plus AI-driven L1 automation. Offshore labor arbitrage is the OLD margin lever that this plan's own AI thesis makes obsolete, it clashes with the trust/compliance expectations of the target vertical, and it depresses the exit multiple consolidators will pay. Onshore, relationship-run delivery is the fit; offshore earnings are lower quality and less transferable even when the multiple looks cheap.

concentrationRule.note: No client over ~15% of revenue; 20+ active clients with a broad, diversified mix. SBA lenders treat customer concentration as a documented decline reason — a single client above ~20-25% often needs mitigation or sinks the loan. Index HIGH on many clients + low top-client %.

recurringRule.note: 90%+ contractual monthly recurring, per-seat. Index HIGH on recurring; project / install / staff-aug / one-time revenue is discounted — by consolidators at exit AND by SBA underwriting on the way in.

sbaUnderwriting.note: Deal 1 must clear SBA 7(a) underwriting, not just the buy box. What underwriters test — the scanner flags each:
criteria: DSCR >= ~1.15x (lenders often want 1.25x+) on the acquisition debt — cash flow must cover debt service with cushion
Customer concentration — a top client over ~20-25% of revenue is a documented decline reason; diversified many-client revenue is strongly preferred
Recurring vs. project revenue — contractual MRR is credited; one-time / project / install revenue is discounted
Quality of earnings — aggressive add-backs are normalized down; the supportable loan is set on defensible cash flow, not headline adjusted EBITDA
Independent business valuation — SBA will not finance above appraised value, so a consolidator-priced ask cannot be SBA-funded at that number
Transferability — the business must run without the seller (involvement capped ~12 months); a GM who owns relationships is what makes it bankable
Buyer qualification / industry experience; min 10% equity injection (up to half can be a seller note on full 2-yr standby); personal guarantee from 20%+ owners
